subject: ventures/cra-evidence-desk
professional: a product-security (PSIRT) lead at a software vendor preparing for EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) Article 14 reporting; first checks: does an SBOM-vs-advisory match report every advisory that names a component (no silent drops), do real purl/OSV spellings meet (PyPI PEP 503 names, Go 'v' versions, apk/deb vs Alpine/Debian), is 'not evaluated' coverage disclosed, and are the Article 14 deadlines, recipients and notification contents stated as the regulation states them.

evidence.correctness: Independent script /tmp/claude-0/audit-cra-evidence-desk/indep.py (expected values from the purl spec, OSV schema and PEP 503; subject run only through its CLI) on 8 cases: 2 pass, 6 fail. Maven namespace/name vs OSV group:artifact and npm %40-scoped purls match (pass). FAIL: two real advisories enumerating lodash 4.17.15 (GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw, GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) give 1 finding, not 2: core.match indexes advisories in a dict keyed by (ecosystem,name,version) so the last one overwrites the first, and the browser port (site/match.mjs:256, Map.set) does the same (node /tmp/claude-0/audit-cra-evidence-desk/browser.mjs -> 1 ['GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm']). A component named by several advisories is the normal case (log4j-core 2.14.1 has CVE-2021-44228 and CVE-2021-45046), so the evidence record silently omits advisories a user would act on. FAIL: pkg:pypi/typing-extensions vs OSV PyPI typing_extensions (PEP 503 equivalent) no match; pkg:golang/...@v0.7.0 vs OSV Go version 0.7.0 no match (OSV Go SEMVER has no 'v'); pkg:apk/alpine/openssl vs OSV Alpine:v3.19 no match; an OSV record with one enumerated package and one range-only package is not listed under advisories_not_evaluated; advisory_count reports 4 for 2 records (it counts enumerated versions). Example fixtures reproduce (CLI JSON on examples/*.osv.json: 1 finding, 1 not evaluated).
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end: CycloneDX, SPDX and native SBOMs; OSV (bare/vulns) and native advisories; purl folding; nested sub-components; advisories_not_evaluated; JSON and draft output; usage counter; browser page with example. Live page: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs cra-evidence-desk` -> no placeholder or retired origin. No stubs/TODOs. The 'golang vs Go meet' claim is hollow in practice because versions differ by the 'v' prefix.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q`: 24 passed in 0.21 s; `cd site && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 69 pass. quality_mutate.py, 5 mutants, 2 survived: dropping .lower() from the component key (core.py:25) and from the browser key (site/match.mjs:261) both leave every test green. Caught: has_ranges and not has_exact -> has_ranges (normalize.py:297), maven ':' separator -> '/' (normalize.py:75), dropping the OSV distribution qualifier split (normalize.py:68). No test supplies two advisories for one component, which is how the dedup defect shipped.
evidence.craft: Read core.py (69), cli.py (65), normalize.py (302), site/match.mjs (362), test_*.py, parity.test.mjs. Clean, well-commented stdlib code; malformed purls skipped not raised; usage counter robust to corrupt files. Defects: last-wins dict index (core.py:22); report() normalises SBOM and advisories twice; the engine is duplicated in JS, mitigated by parity.test.mjs reading the Python ECOSYSTEM_ALIASES table, but parity does not cover match semantics; advisory_count is a count of version entries labelled as advisories.
evidence.claims: Checked: nothing uploaded (pass, match.mjs reads File locally); exact match only, ranges listed not dropped (pass for whole-record range-only; partial for mixed records); CycloneDX/SPDX/OSV accepted (pass); golang/Go and cargo/crates.io fold (ecosystem pass, Go versions fail); disclaimer and no-warranty on page, README and CLI epilog (pass); Art 14 start date 11 September 2026 (pass, Art 71(2)); applies to products already on the market (pass, Art 69(3)); 24 h / 72 h (pass, Art 14(2)(a),(b) and 14(4)(a),(b)). FAIL: index.html:36 and :243 say the final report for an actively exploited vulnerability is due '14 days ... after the 72-hour notification'; Art 14(2)(c) says no later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available (the one-month incident deadline after the notification, Art 14(4)(c), is right). It says 'must notify ENISA'; Art 14(1)/(3) require notification to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and to ENISA simultaneously via the single reporting platform (Art 16). vs-dependency-track.html says the draft is 'built around that one document', but the draft carries none of the Art 14(2)/(4) content headings.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a vendor with a syft CycloneDX SBOM and an osv.dev export wants the list of advisories naming their components and a draft for counsel. Works for npm/Maven with enumerated versions. A Go, PyPI-with-underscores or Alpine/Debian SBOM gets false 'no match'; a component with several advisories loses all but one; the draft has to be rewritten into Art 14 shape by hand. Usable as a first pass, not as the evidence record it is sold as.
evidence.domain: Compared against Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Art 14(1)-(4), 16, 69(3), 71(2), and OSV/purl practice. Departures: an advisory match is neither an 'actively exploited vulnerability' (14(1)) nor a 'severe incident' (14(3)), yet the draft is titled 'INCIDENT NOTIFICATION' and conflates the two; the draft lacks 14(2)/(4) content (Member States where the product is made available, general nature of the exploit, corrective or mitigating measures taken and available to users, sensitivity of the information); final-report timing misstated for vulnerabilities; name/version normalisation below what OSV-Scanner or Dependency-Track do (PEP 503, Go 'v').

defects.what: A component named by more than one advisory is reported with only the last advisory: match() indexes advisories in a dict/Map keyed by (ecosystem,name,version), so earlier advisories are overwritten and silently missing from the evidence record and the Article 14 draft (lodash 4.17.15 with two GHSAs -> 1 finding). Same in the browser port.

Page states the actively-exploited-vulnerability final report is due 14 days after the 72-hour notification; Art 14(2)(c) sets 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available. It also says notifications go to ENISA, where Art 14(1)/(3) and 16 require the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA via the single reporting platform.
Go components never match: purl versions keep the 'v' prefix (v0.7.0) and OSV Go versions do not (0.7.0); the README's 'golang vs Go' folding claim only fixes the ecosystem.
PyPI names are compared by lowercasing only; PEP 503 treats '-', '_' and '.' as equivalent, so typing-extensions (purl) vs typing_extensions (OSV) misses.

Ecosystem table lacks purl apk/deb/rpm vs OSV Alpine/Debian/Red Hat spellings, so OS-package SBOMs from syft/trivy never meet OSV distro advisories, despite the code comment claiming Alpine qualifier handling makes them meet.
An OSV record with an enumerated package and a range-only package is not listed in advisories_not_evaluated, though the range-only package was never evaluated; a clean report overstates coverage.

Article 14 draft has none of the content Art 14(2)(b)/(4)(b) asks for (Member States where made available, general nature of the exploit/vulnerability, corrective or mitigating measures, sensitivity) and is titled 'INCIDENT NOTIFICATION' for what is at most a vulnerability lead; vs-dependency-track.html calls it 'built around that one document'.
advisory_count counts enumerated version entries, not advisories (2 records -> 4).
Case-insensitive name matching is untested: removing .lower() from the component key survives both suites (Python and browser).

verdict: Clean, honest-in-intent local matcher with a good disclaimer and a real coverage disclosure, but its core output is wrong in the common case: a component named by several advisories keeps only the last one (recomputed with two real lodash GHSAs: 1 finding, expected 2), in both the CLI and the page. Purl/OSV folding misses Go versions, PyPI PEP 503 names and distro packages; the page misstates the Art 14(2)(c) final-report deadline; the draft is not shaped to Art 14's content. Below the bar on correctness, claims and verification (2 of 5 mutants survived).
